# Pick My Costume: full build-guide corpus

> Complete Markdown text of pickmycostume.com's 169 Halloween costume build guides,
> generated from the site's idea bank on the date below. Free, no signup, no ads.
> Generated: 2026-10-26. Regenerate with gen_llms_full.py when the bank changes.

## Site summary

- Pick My Costume (https://pickmycostume.com/) is a free Halloween costume idea finder.
- 169 costume ideas. Every idea has a materials list and numbered step-by-step build instructions.
- 16 of the 169 ideas need zero to two supplies beyond default household basics (pantry audit, Oct 2026).
- Licensed characters are deliberately excluded from the bank.

## All 169 build guides

### Amazon Warrior

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/amazon-warrior

Red, blue, and gold with star accents and cuff bracelets: battle-ready like a kid goddess.

Build time, effort: 40 min / Easy

Materials:
- Red top, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Blue shorts or skirt, 1 (own)
- Gold craft foam for cuffs, 1 sheet (buy: craft store)
- Gold star stickers, 1 pack (buy: craft store)
- Red headband, 1 (own, or buy: dollar store)
- Gold and red non-toxic face paint, 1 set (buy: toy store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Pull on the red top and the blue shorts or skirt.
2. Cut two wide cuffs from the gold craft foam.
3. Tape the cuffs closed around the wrists.
4. Stick gold star stickers across the red top.
5. Stick one gold star on each cheek.
6. Safety: keep face paint clear of the eyes, and keep the foam cuffs loose enough to slide a finger underneath.
7. Paint one bold stripe of red and gold across one cheek.
8. Pull on the red headband.
9. Optional pro finish: cut a gold star from leftover foam and glue it to the headband.

Q: What if I cannot find gold craft foam?
A: Cut the cuffs from cardboard and cover them in gold stickers or yellow tape. The shape reads as cuffs before the color does.

Q: How do the cuffs stay on?
A: Tape each cuff into a loose tube that slides over the hand. Snug enough to stay, loose enough to slide off fast.

### Astronaut

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/astronaut

White sweats, a paper-bag helmet, and a flag patch.

Build time, effort: 25 min / Easy

Materials:
- White sweatshirt and sweatpants, 1 set (buy: clothing store, or use your own)
- 1 large brown paper grocery bag (buy: grocery store or craft store)
- Silver duct tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
- Flag sticker or iron-on patch, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut the face hole small first. You can widen it later.
2. Hold the bag up to the face and trace the opening first.
3. Wrap two silver tape stripes around each sleeve.
4. Wrap two silver tape stripes around each pant leg.
5. Press the flag sticker onto the chest.
6. Safety: Cut the face opening wide enough that vision and hearing stay clear.
7. Pull on the white sweatshirt and sweatpants.
8. Slip the bag over your head.
9. Line up the face hole.
10. Crimp the top with a strip of duct tape.
11. Optional pro finish: print a mission patch and tape it to the other side of the chest.

Q: What size paper bag fits a kid astronaut helmet?
A: A standard large brown grocery bag fits kids and most adults. For a toddler, use a small paper gift bag and cut the face opening to match their face.

Q: How do you keep the paper bag helmet from slipping?
A: Crimp the top of the bag with a strip of duct tape so it holds its shape, and cut the face opening wide enough that it sits on the shoulders, not the head.

---

### Baby Dinosaur

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/baby-dino

Green hoodie, felt spikes down the back, stuffed tail.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Green hoodie, 1 (buy: clothing store, or use your own)
- 2 sheets green craft felt, 9x12 inches each (buy: craft store, construction paper works too)
- Pillow stuffing or 2 old socks (make: stuff from home)
- Safety pins, 6 to 8 (buy: dollar store)
- Masking tape, 1 roll
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut a paper triangle first.
2. Test the size on the hoodie.
3. Cut 6 to 8 big triangles from the green felt.
4. Tape the spikes in a row down the back of the hoodie.
5. Pin each spike from inside the hoodie.
6. Stuff the old socks with the pillow stuffing.
7. Tape the open ends of the socks shut.
8. Safety: Pin everything from inside the green hoodie, so pin backs face the fabric and never the skin.
9. Pin the stuffed tail to the back waistband of the hoodie.
10. Optional pro finish: cut two small white felt triangles and pin them to the cuffs as claws.

Q: How many spikes does a baby dinosaur need?
A: Six to eight palm-size triangles down the back reads as dinosaur instantly. Fewer looks sparse; more looks cluttered.

Q: How do you make a dinosaur tail that stays up?
A: Stuff two old socks firmly with pillow stuffing, tape the open ends shut, and pin the tail to the back waistband, not higher, or it flops forward.

---

### Baby Pumpkin

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/baby-pumpkin

An orange onesie, green felt leaves, and the easiest first Halloween ever.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Orange onesie or footed pajamas, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Green craft felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Soft stuffing or an old pillow, 1 (own)
- Brown felt for the stem, 1 small piece (buy: craft store)
- Safety pins, 4 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Lightly stuff the onesie arms and legs.
2. Cut leaf shapes from the green felt.
3. Pin the leaves around the collar.
4. Roll the brown felt into a stem.
5. Pin the stem to the top of the hood or a soft hat.
6. Safety: Keep all pins on the outside of the onesie where you can see them, and never pin near the baby's skin. Skip small parts a baby could pull off.
7. Optional pro finish: photograph the pumpkin in a laundry basket lined with a blanket.

Q: How do you keep a baby warm in just a onesie?
A: Layer a long-sleeve shirt and tights underneath. The stuffing goes between the layers, never against the skin.

Q: What if the baby hates the stem hat?
A: Skip the hat. The orange onesie and leaves alone still read as pumpkin in every photo.

---

### Backyard Superhero

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/backyard-hero

Short cape plus a first initial on the chest, mask optional.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- Old pillowcase or t-shirt for the cape, 1 (make: cut up)
- Solid-color t-shirt to wear, 1 (own)
- Cardstock or foam letter for the first initial, 1 sheet (make: cut from cardstock, or buy: craft store)
- Ribbon or string for cape ties, about 2 feet (own, or buy: craft store)
- Safety pins, 2
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Hold the pillowcase against the back.
2. Mark waist length.
3. Cut the cape.
4. Leave it long; trim it after a fitting.
5. Cut the first initial from the cardstock.
6. Pin the initial to the chest of the t-shirt.
7. Safety: Keep the neck bow loose and easy to pull free. Never tie anything tight around the neck.
8. Thread the ribbon through the top corners of the cape.
9. Tie the ribbon at the neck in a loose bow.
10. Trim the ribbon ends.
11. Optional pro finish: outline the initial with a fabric marker in a bold color.

Q: How long should a kid superhero cape be?
A: Waist length for under-6s (no tripping), mid-back for older kids. When in doubt, cut long and trim after they try it on.

Q: How do you attach a cape without sewing?
A: Thread ribbon through the top corners and tie a loose quick-release bow at the front of the neck. Never tie it tight, it must pull free.

### Bacon & Eggs

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/bacon-eggs

Wavy bacon stripes and a sunny-side-up egg yolk.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Dark red or brown shirt for the bacon, 1 (own)
- White shirt for the egg, 1 (own)
- 1 sheet red-brown craft felt, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, construction paper works too)
- 1 sheet each white and yellow craft felt, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, construction paper works too)
- Safety pins, 6 to 8 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Lay the felt on the shirts.
2. Pin the layout before you cut.
3. Cut 4 wavy strips from the red-brown felt.
4. Cut one large white oval from the felt.
5. Cut one yellow circle from the felt.
6. Pin the wavy strips down the front of the dark shirt.
7. Pin the white oval to the white shirt.
8. Pin the yellow circle on top of the oval.
9. Safety: Pin from inside the shirt. Pin backs must face cloth, not skin.
10. Put on the shirts.
11. For photos, the bacon stands just behind the egg.
12. Optional pro finish: cut the bacon strips with a wavy line, not straight.

Q: How do you make the fried egg read clearly?
A: Scale is everything: the white oval should cover most of the shirt chest, with the yellow yolk circle about a third of its size, pinned on top center.

Q: Will safety pins hold felt all night?
A: Yes if you pin from inside the shirt so the pin backs face the fabric. Use two pins per strip for the bacon so nothing rotates.

---

### Ballerina

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/ballerina

A tulle tutu tied onto elastic, a leotard, and a neat ballerina bun.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Pink tulle, 2 to 3 yards (buy: craft store)
- Wide elastic, 1 inch wide, cut to the waist size plus 1 inch overlap (buy: craft store)
- Pink leotard or fitted shirt, 1 (own, or buy: clothing store)
- Pink tights, 1 pair (own, or buy: clothing store)
- Hair ties and bobby pins, 1 pack (own)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Satin ribbon, 1 short length (optional, for the pro finish; buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Wrap the elastic snug around the waist.
2. Overlap 1 inch and cut.
3. Tie the overlap into a loop.
4. This is the waistband.
5. Cut the tulle into strips about 3 inches wide.
6. Make each strip twice as long as the skirt.
7. Fold one strip in half to make a loop.
8. Slip the loop under the elastic.
9. Pull the strip ends through the loop.
10. Pull tight.
11. Repeat all the way around, about 30 to 40 strips.
12. Fluff the strips outward.
13. Trim the bottom edge even while the tutu hangs.
14. Safety: The elastic should sit snug on the waist, not the hips, so it stays up while twirling. Nothing tied around the neck.
15. Wear the tutu over the leotard and tights.
16. Pull the hair into a high bun.
17. Optional pro finish: pin a small ribbon bow at the back waistband.

Q: How much tulle for a no-sew tutu?
A: 2 yards for a toddler, 3 for a bigger kid. Cut strips 3 inches wide, with length equal to twice the finished skirt length.

Q: How do you keep a no-sew tutu from falling down?
A: Measure the elastic snug at the waist (not the hips) with a 1-inch overlap, and tie strips tight against each other so the weight stays balanced.

---

### Bamboo-Muzzle Demon

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/bamboo-demon

Pink robe, long dark wig, and a cardboard bamboo muzzle tied with ribbon.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Pink bathrobe or kimono-style robe, 1 (own, or buy: clothing store)
- Long dark wig, 1 (buy: toy store or online)
- 1 cardboard tube from wrapping paper or paper towels (make: save from home)
- Ribbon or string, about 3 feet (own, or buy: craft store)
- Red non-toxic face paint, 1 tube (buy: toy store)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Tape, 1 roll

Steps:
1. Hold the tube against the face.
2. Mark chin width.
3. Cut the tube a little long. You can trim it later.
4. Tape a length of ribbon to each end of the tube.
5. Safety: Keep the knot loose enough to talk and breathe easily. Never tie anything tight around the head or neck.
6. Tie the tube across the mouth.
7. Knot it loosely at the back.
8. Pull on the pink bathrobe.
9. Put on the long dark wig.
10. Dab a small red mouth mark on the tube.
11. Optional pro finish: draw bamboo lines along the tube with a brown marker.

Q: How do you keep the muzzle comfortable?
A: Tie the ribbon loosely at the back of the head with a bow, not a knot, so it can be loosened fast. It should rest against the mouth, never press on it.

Q: What can I use instead of a wig?
A: A dark towel draped over the head works for photos. The robe and muzzle carry the costume; the wig is optional.

### Banana

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/banana

Yellow sweatsuit with a green felt stem hat.

Build time, effort: 10 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Yellow sweatshirt and sweatpants, 1 set (buy: at a clothing store, or own: from closet)
- Green felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Put on the yellow sweatshirt and sweatpants.
2. Cut a stem shape from green felt, about 4 inches tall.
3. Safety: Let an adult cut the felt stem. Keep fingers clear of the scissors.
4. Hold the stem against the headband.
5. Check it in a mirror.
6. Glue the stem to the headband.
7. Let it dry flat.
8. Wear the headband.
9. You are a banana.
10. Optional pro finish: glue a small brown felt tip at the bottom front of the sweatshirt.

Q: How big should the banana stem be?
A: About 4 inches tall and 2 inches wide. Bigger looks cartoonish in a good way; smaller disappears.

Q: Can I make this with zero shopping?
A: Yes if you own yellow sweats: cut the stem from a green t-shirt or paper bag painted green, and tape it to any headband or hat.

---

### Basketball Star

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/basketball-star

Jersey, shorts, eye-black stripes, and a ball that never leaves your hand.

Build time, effort: 5 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Basketball jersey or numbered tank top, 1 (own, or buy: sporting goods store)
- Basketball shorts, 1 pair (own)
- Black non-toxic face paint or 1 eyeliner pencil (buy: toy store)
- Basketball, 1 (own, or buy: toy store)

Steps:
1. Pull on the basketball jersey and shorts.
2. Safety: Use only the black non-toxic face paint. Skip the eye black for very young kids who will rub their eyes.
3. Draw two short black stripes under each eye.
4. Keep the stripes below the eye, never on the eyelid.
5. Skip the stripes for kids who rub their eyes.
6. Carry the basketball tucked under one arm.
7. Dribble it whenever you stand still.
8. Optional pro finish: add a wristband and tall socks.

Q: Do I need a real jersey?
A: No. Any numbered tank top works, write a big number on a plain shirt with a fabric marker and it reads the same from ten feet away.

Q: Is eye black safe for kids?
A: Use only non-toxic face paint marketed for kids, keep it below the eye, and skip it for very young kids who rub their eyes.

### Beekeeper & Bee

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/beekeeper-bee

One goes as the beekeeper in white with a mesh veil; the other wears yellow and black stripes with antennae.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- White long-sleeve shirt and white pants, 1 set (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Fine mesh fabric or a mosquito head net, 1 (buy: craft store or camping aisle)
- Wide-brim hat, 1 (own, or buy: dollar store)
- Yellow shirt and yellow pants, 1 set (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Black electrical tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
- Black pipe cleaners for antennae, 2 (buy: craft store)
- Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store, or use your own)
- Yellow and black face paint sticks, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Beekeeper: drape the mesh over the hat.
2. Tie it at the neck.
3. Cut the face opening wide first.
4. Trim it after a fitting.
5. Bee: wrap 3 to 4 black tape stripes around the yellow shirt and pants.
6. Press the tape flat so the edges stay down.
7. Bend the pipe cleaners into a V.
8. Tape them to the headband for antennae.
9. Add two black face-paint dots on the cheeks.
10. Safety: Cut the veil opening wide enough that vision stays clear, and tie nothing tight around the neck. Use tape, not string, for the stripes so nothing unravels.
11. The adult is the beekeeper, since the mesh limits vision.
12. The smaller of the two is the bee.
13. Optional pro finish: the beekeeper carries a small cardboard sign that says HONEY.

Q: How do you make a beekeeper veil you can see through?
A: Use fine mesh fabric or a mosquito head net draped over a wide-brim hat, with the face opening cut wide and the fabric tied at the neck, never taped to the skin.

Q: Will the black tape stripes stay on all night?
A: Press electrical tape flat onto clean, dry fabric and it holds for an evening. For a longer night, use black felt strips with fabric glue instead.

### Black Cat Burglar

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/black-cat

Black sweatsuit, cat-ear headband, eye mask. Add a toy sack for burglar.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Black shirt and pants or sweatsuit, 1 set (own)
- Plain headband, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- 1 sheet black craft felt, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, construction paper works too)
- Black construction paper, 1 sheet (make: cut a mask from it)
- Black non-toxic face paint, 1 tube (buy: toy store)
- Small drawstring bag or pillowcase, 1 (own)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Tape, 1 roll

Steps:
1. Cut two triangle ears from the black felt, about 4 inches tall.
2. Cut one eye mask shape from the black paper.
3. Tape the ears upright to the headband.
4. Safety: Cut the eye holes wide in the mask so vision stays clear.
5. Tape the mask on with tape tabs at the temples.
6. Or draw whiskers with the black face paint.
7. Pull on the black shirt and pants.
8. Put on the headband.
9. Carry the small drawstring bag over one shoulder.
10. Optional pro finish: tape three pipe cleaners to each cheek as whiskers.

Q: How do you make cat ears stand up?
A: Cut the triangles 4 inches tall and tape them to the headband with a 1-inch tape tab folded over the band on both sides. Felt alone flops; the double-sided tape tab is the trick.

Q: Mask or face paint whiskers for a toddler?
A: Face paint. A paper mask slips on small faces and the eye holes never line up. Paint three whisker lines per cheek and skip the mask.

### Block Game Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/block-game-crew

Cardboard-box heads: pick your blocky hero.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- 1 large cardboard box per person, big enough to fit over the torso (make: ask a grocery store for spares)
- Acrylic paint in each hero's colors, 1 small bottle per color (buy: craft store, tempera paint works too)
- Paintbrushes, 1 wide and 1 detail per person
- Black marker, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Each person picks a blocky video-game hero look.
2. Safety: An adult should handle the heavy cutting, and cut the eye holes generously so everyone can see clearly.
3. Measure each person's head and shoulders first.
4. Cut a head opening and eye holes in each box.
5. Cut the head opening smaller than you think. Cardboard cannot be put back.
6. Cut the eye holes wide so everyone can see clearly.
7. Paint each box in the hero's main colors.
8. Let it dry fully.
9. Draw a square face and details on the front of each box.
10. Wear the boxes over regular clothes once the paint is dry.
11. Optional pro finish: draw thin black grid lines across the painted box.

Q: How do you keep a box costume comfortable?
A: Cut arm holes wide, wear it over regular clothes, and tape the inside edges of every cut so cardboard never scratches. Keep the box at torso height, never over the face, for kids.

Q: How long does the paint take to dry?
A: Acrylic on cardboard needs about 1 hour to stop being tacky. Paint the night before if you can; wearing it damp smears the pixel face.

---

### Block Monster

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/block-monster

Wear all one solid color, square up your silhouette with foam or cardboard blocks on shoulders/limbs, draw a pixelated face.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Solid-color sweatsuit, any color, 1 set (own)
- 1 large cardboard box (make: cut it into square blocks)
- Packing tape, 1 roll
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Non-toxic face paint, 1 tube (buy: toy store)

Steps:
1. Cut the box into square blocks: two large, four medium.
2. Test-hold each block against the body before taping.
3. Tape one large block to each shoulder.
4. Tape one medium block to each forearm and shin.
5. Pull on the solid-color sweatsuit under the blocks.
6. Safety: Keep the face paint clear of the eyes.
7. Draw a blocky square-toothed grin with the face paint.
8. Optional pro finish: edge every block with silver duct tape.

Q: How do the blocks stay on?
A: Packing tape loops: tape the block to the sweatsuit sleeve or pant leg with two strips. Tape sticks to fabric well enough for one evening and peels off after.

Q: What size blocks for a small kid?
A: Halve everything: medium blocks become the shoulder blocks. Oversized blocks on a small kid drag and bump doorways.

### Blue Alien Ohana

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/blue-alien-ohana

A blue hoodie and an antenna headband turn the kid into the alien.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Blue hoodie per alien-role person, 1 each (own, or buy: clothing store)
- Blue pipe cleaners, 2 per alien (buy: craft store)
- Blue pom-poms, 2 per alien (buy: craft store)
- Headband per alien-role person, 1 each (buy: dollar store)
- Red t-shirt or dress per Lilo-role person, 1 each (make: from closet, or buy: thrift store)
- White craft felt or paper, 1 sheet (buy: craft store)
- Safety pins, 4 to 6 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Tape, 1 roll

Steps:
1. Wrap each headband in blue tape.
2. Twist two blue pipe cleaners around the top of each headband.
3. Bend each tip into a small curl.
4. Tape one blue pom-pom to the tip of each pipe cleaner.
5. Safety: Under 3: skip the pom-pom antennae, toddlers can pull them off and they are a choking hazard. The blue hoodie alone carries the costume.
6. Pull on the blue hoodies.
7. Lilo: cut leaf shapes from the white felt or paper.
8. Pin or glue the leaves across the red t-shirt or dress.
9. Safety: Pin from the front of the red shirt, so pin backs face the fabric and never the skin.
10. Wear dark hair down for Lilo.
11. Put the antenna headbands on the aliens last.
12. Optional pro finish: twist each pipe cleaner into a loose zigzag before adding the pom-pom.

Q: How do you keep the antennae from flopping?
A: Twist each pipe cleaner around the headband twice at the base before standing it up, the double wrap is the anchor. Then tape over the twist. Pipe cleaner alone flops by hour two; the tape wrap locks it.

Q: What if we only have one blue hoodie?
A: Make the second alien a different blue: navy t-shirt plus blue face paint on the arms. The antenna headbands match, so the pair still reads.

### Aussie Dog Family

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/blue-dog-family

Dog-ear headbands and blue-or-orange shirts: mama, dad, and the pups.

Build time, effort: 25 min / Easy

Materials:
- Blue or orange t-shirt per person, 1 each (own, or buy: clothing store)
- Headband per person, 1 each (buy: dollar store)
- Blue, orange, and white craft felt, 1 sheet of each color 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, construction paper works too)
- Safety pins, 4 per person (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut one paper ear first.
2. Check it against the headband.
3. Cut two floppy felt ears for each person, about 5 inches long.
4. Match ear color to shirt color.
5. Pin the ears to each headband.
6. Pin a white felt belly spot to the front of each t-shirt.
7. Safety: Pin ears and spots from inside. Pin backs must face cloth, not skin.
8. Pull on the blue or orange t-shirts.
9. Put on the headbands.
10. Decide who is mama, dad, and the pups.
11. Optional pro finish: stuff an old sock with tissue and pin it at the back waistband as a tail.

Q: How do you tell the family members apart?
A: Match the show: blue shirt for the dad dog, orange for the mom dog, mix for the pups. Add a white belly spot to the pups only, the audience reads it instantly.

Q: Ears keep sliding off the headband. Fix?
A: Pin the ears to the headband with two safety pins each instead of tape. Pins survive hugs; tape gives up by the second photo.

### Blue Heeler Pup

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/blue-heeler-pup

Blue-gray hoodie, felt ears, and a painted nose for the littlest pup.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Blue-gray hoodie, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Blue-gray sweatpants, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Blue and dark gray craft felt, 1 sheet each 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Black face paint or eyeliner, 1 (own)
- Safety pins, 4 (buy: dollar store)
- Fabric glue, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut two triangle ears from the blue felt.
2. Glue the ears to a strip that pins inside the hood.
3. Glue dark gray felt spots onto the hoodie and one pant leg.
4. Paint a black nose and whisker dots on the child's face.
5. Pin a short felt tail to the back of the sweatpants.
6. Pin from inside so pin backs face the fabric.
7. Safety: Use face paint, never a mask, on small kids so they can see and breathe easily, and keep pins inside the clothes.
8. Optional pro finish: teach the pup one trick, like sitting for a treat.

Q: How do you keep the ears up on the hood?
A: Glue each ear to a small cardboard triangle first, then pin the triangles inside the hood. Felt alone flops.

Q: What if the kid will not keep the hood up?
A: Pin the ears to a soft headband instead. The hood stays down and the ears still read.

### Board Game Pieces

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/board-game-pieces

Each person picks a piece: cardboard die, playing card, pawn, or domino over monochrome clothes.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- Black or white monochrome clothes, 1 set per person (own)
- Large cardboard boxes, 2 to 3 (make: collect spares)
- White and black acrylic paint, 1 small bottle each (buy: craft store, tempera paint works too)
- Paintbrushes, 1 wide and 1 detail
- Black marker, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Ribbon or string for straps, about 4 feet per board (own)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Tape, 1 roll

Steps:
1. Each person picks a game piece to be.
2. Sketch each piece on the cardboard before cutting.
3. Cut a cube shape from a large box for the die.
4. Measure the head first.
5. Cut the opening small, then widen.
6. Cut flat boards from another box for the card and the domino.
7. Paint the die and card white and the domino black.
8. Let the paint dry fully.
9. Add dots and card symbols with the marker.
10. Safety: Cut the die box eye holes generously so you can see clearly. Only wear the die box once all paint is fully dry.
11. Tape ribbon straps to the flat boards.
12. Hang the boards front and back over plain clothes.
13. Wear the die box over the head with the eye holes lined up.
14. Optional pro finish: paint a thin gold border around the card and domino edges.

Q: Which game pieces are easiest to recognize?
A: The die (white cube, black dots), a playing card (white board, big red heart), and a domino (black board, white dots). Pick pieces with strong silhouettes.

Q: How do flat boards stay on?
A: Tape ribbon straps to the top corners so they hang front and back like a sandwich board over the monochrome clothes. Two straps, not one, so nothing spins.

---

### Bowling Pins

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/bowling-pins

White outfits with red neck stripes, plus one bowler in black.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- White shirt and pants per pin person, 1 set each (own)
- Red duct or electrical tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
- Black shirt and pants for the bowler, 1 set (own)
- Toy bowling ball or black playground ball, 1 (buy: toy store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Each pin person cuts two red tape stripes from the roll.
2. Cut all stripes before sticking any, so they match.
3. Wrap two red tape stripes around the collar of the white shirt.
4. Wrap one stripe around each wrist.
5. The bowler pulls on the black shirt and pants.
6. Safety: Use a lightweight toy ball, never a real bowling ball.
7. Carry the toy bowling ball.
8. Line the pins up in formation, with the bowler at the end, for photos.
9. Optional pro finish: number the pins 1 through 10 on the back with a marker.

Q: Where exactly do the red stripes go?
A: Two stripes around the collar of the white shirt and one around each wrist. That is the whole pin read, collar plus wrists.

Q: Can the bowler use a real bowling ball?
A: No, use a lightweight toy ball or playground ball painted black. A real ball is a weapon in a crowd and most venues ban them.

### Boxer

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/boxer

Bathrobe, toy gloves, bruise makeup, and entrance music.

Build time, effort: 10 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Bathrobe, 1 (own)
- Toy boxing gloves, 1 pair (buy: toy store)
- Purple and yellow non-toxic face paint, 1 tube each (buy: toy store)
- Athletic shorts and sneakers, 1 set (own)
- Phone for entrance music, 1 (own)

Steps:
1. Pull on the athletic shorts, sneakers, and bathrobe.
2. Hood up.
3. Safety: Keep the face paint clear of the eyes.
4. Dab purple and yellow face paint on one cheekbone and around one eye.
5. Use one bruise only.
6. Five bruises reads as accident.
7. Keep all paint clear of the eyes.
8. Pull on the toy boxing gloves.
9. Throw a few shadow punches.
10. Play entrance music as you walk in.
11. Optional pro finish: write your fighter name across the back of the robe with tape letters.

Q: How do you do bruise makeup that looks real?
A: Layer purple first, then dab yellow at the edges. Real bruises are darkest in the center and yellow at the healing edge. Blend with a fingertip, not a brush.

Q: Toy gloves or real gloves?
A: Toy gloves only. Real boxing gloves are heavy, sweaty, and you cannot hold a drink. Toy gloves photograph identically.

### Breakfast Buffet

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/breakfast-buffet

Everyone picks a breakfast: egg, bacon, toast, pancake, OJ, coffee. Cardboard signs over normal clothes.

Build time, effort: 25 min / Easy

Materials:
- Cardboard sheets, 1 per person about 2x2 feet (make: cut from boxes)
- Markers in assorted colors, 1 pack (own, or buy: dollar store)
- String or yarn, about 4 feet per person (own)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Each person picks a breakfast item.
2. Draw the food on paper first to plan the layout.
3. Cut a large circle or rectangle from the cardboard.
4. Draw the food big on the cardboard.
5. Fill the whole board.
6. Safety: An adult pokes the holes in the top corners with the tip of the scissors, since pushing through cardboard takes force.
7. Thread the string through the holes.
8. Wear the sign over normal clothes like a sandwich board.
9. Optional pro finish: make one small sign that says BREAKFAST BUFFET, all you can eat.

Q: What breakfast foods read best on a sign?
A: Fried egg, bacon strips, and a coffee mug, all three are recognizable in three marker strokes. Pancakes need more detail; skip them unless someone is artistic.

Q: How do you wear a cardboard sign comfortably?
A: Two strings through the top corners, worn like a sandwich board over normal clothes. Keep the board at chest height so it does not bang knees.

### Bumble Bee

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/bumble-bee

Black sweats with yellow tape stripes and soft felt antennae.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Black sweatshirt and sweatpants, 1 set (own, or buy: clothing store)
- Yellow duct or electrical tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
- Black headband, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- 2 yellow pipe cleaners, 12 inches each (buy: craft store, floral wire works too)
- 2 black pom-poms, 1 inch (buy: craft store, cotton balls work too)
- Craft glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Mark stripe spots with chalk or a light pencil first.
2. Wrap three yellow tape stripes around the black sweatshirt.
3. Wrap one stripe around each arm.
4. Twist the two yellow pipe cleaners into a V.
5. Safety: Use non-toxic craft glue, and keep the pom-poms out of reach of toddlers.
6. Glue a black pom-pom to each tip of the V.
7. Glue the base of the V to the black headband.
8. Let the glue dry fully.
9. Pull on the black sweatshirt and sweatpants.
10. Put on the black headband.
11. Optional pro finish: cut two white ovals from a plastic bag and tape them to the back as wings.

Q: Will duct tape stick to a sweatshirt all night?
A: Yes on fleece and cotton. Press each stripe firmly and smooth from the center out. It peels off clean after one evening.

Q: How do you keep the antennae upright?
A: Twist the two pipe cleaners into a tight V and glue the base, not just the tips, to the headband. A wide glued base is what keeps them vertical.

### Burger & Fries

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/burger-fries

Sesame-seed bun top for one, red fry carton with yellow fry sticks for the other.

Build time, effort: 35 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Tan t-shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Red t-shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Green, red, and yellow craft felt, 1 sheet each 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Tan felt for the bun top, 1 sheet (buy: craft store)
- Paper bowl for the bun, 1 large (buy: grocery store)
- Cardboard for the fry carton, 1 sheet (make: from a shipping box)
- Red acrylic paint or red paper, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Yellow paper for fry sticks (buy: dollar store, or make: from paper)
- Tape, 1 roll
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Buy the felt, bowl, and paint.
2. Pull a tan and a red t-shirt from the closet.
3. Burger: cut wavy felt strips.
4. Green for lettuce, red for tomato, yellow for cheese.
5. Glue the strips in a stack across the tan t-shirt.
6. Cover the paper bowl with tan felt.
7. Wear the bowl upside down as the bun top.
8. Fries: fold the cardboard into an open-top carton.
9. Paint it red.
10. Or cover the carton with red paper.
11. Let it dry.
12. Cut yellow paper into fry sticks.
13. Glue the sticks poking out of the carton top.
14. Wear the carton like a sandwich board over the red t-shirt.
15. Use ribbon straps over the shoulders.
16. Safety: Round the cardboard corners, and keep the fry sticks soft paper, never wood, so the carton is crowd-safe.
17. Optional pro finish: drop real wrapped candy into the fry carton.

Q: How do you keep the bun bowl on your head?
A: Wear it tilted back like a hat, not balanced on top. A strip of double-sided tape inside the rim keeps it put.

Q: Can the fry carton hold real candy?
A: Yes, line it with a plastic bag first so grease never touches the cardboard, and keep it to wrapped candy.

### Burger Joint Couple

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/burger-joint-couple

White apron plus fake mustache, curly red wig plus glasses. Burger shop owners.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- 2 white aprons (buy: dollar store or online)
- Fake mustache, 1 (buy: toy store)
- Curly red wig, 1 (buy: toy store or online)
- Costume glasses, 1 pair (buy: toy store)
- Order pad and pencil, 1 set (own, or buy: dollar store)

Steps:
1. Test the mustache spot in a mirror before peeling the adhesive.
2. One partner pulls on a white apron.
3. Stick on the fake mustache with its skin-safe adhesive.
4. The other partner pulls on the second apron, the curly red wig, and the costume glasses.
5. Carry the order pad and pencil.
6. Take each other's orders all night.
7. Remove the fake mustache gently at the end of the night.
8. Optional pro finish: write BURGER JOINT on both aprons with a red fabric marker.

Q: How do you keep a fake mustache on all night?
A: Clean the skin first (no moisturizer), press for 30 seconds, and carry the adhesive for touch-ups. It loosens after eating, re-press in the bathroom.

Q: What if the wig is itchy?
A: Wear a thin headband or bandana underneath. The barrier layer is the difference between wearing it all night and ripping it off by nine.

### Butterfly

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/butterfly

Painted cardboard wings on black sweats: the garden's prettiest visitor.

Build time, effort: 40 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- Large cardboard for wings, 1 sheet about 3x2 feet (make: from a shipping box)
- Acrylic paint set, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Black sweatsuit, 1 set (own, or buy: clothing store)
- Elastic for wing straps, about 2 feet (buy: craft store)
- Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store, or use your own)
- Pipe cleaners for antennae, 2 (buy: craft store)
- Tape, 1 roll
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Draw one wing on paper.
2. Cut it out.
3. Trace it flipped for the second wing.
4. Cut two big wing shapes from the cardboard.
5. Paint both wings with bright patterns.
6. Let them dry flat.
7. Tape elastic loops to the back of each wing.
8. Bend pipe cleaners into antennae.
9. Tape them to the headband.
10. Safety: Keep wing edges away from doorways; turn sideways to pass through.
11. Wear the wings over the black sweats.
12. Put on the antennae headband.
13. Optional pro finish: outline the wing patterns with glitter glue after the paint dries.

Q: How big should butterfly wings be?
A: Wingtip to wingtip about as wide as the wearer's arm span. Bigger looks majestic in photos but will not fit through doorways, turn sideways.

Q: How do you attach wings so they stay up?
A: Tape two elastic loops to the back of each wing and slip arms through like a backpack. Elastic, not ribbon, it flexes when they move.

### Caped Duo

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/caped-duo

Matching sheet capes, felt masks, and your own emblems.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- 2 old twin sheets or large fabric rectangles, about 4x5 feet each (make: cut from old sheets)
- Craft felt for masks and emblems, 2 sheets 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, construction paper works too)
- Ribbon or cord for cape ties, about 3 feet per cape (own, or buy: craft store)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Paper and pencil for sketching, 1 set (own)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Sketch a matching emblem for each of you on paper.
2. Cut the paper emblems.
3. Hold them against the cape to check the size.
4. Cut the emblems from the craft felt.
5. Cut each sheet into a cape, hem-side down.
6. Glue a felt emblem to the back of each cape.
7. Cut two eye masks from the craft felt.
8. Cut the eye holes wide.
9. Glue ribbon ties to the mask ends.
10. Let the glue dry.
11. Safety: Tie the cord in a loose bow that pulls free easily. Never tie anything tight around the neck. Keep the mask eye holes wide so vision stays clear.
12. Tie the capes at the neck in a loose bow.
13. Put on the masks.
14. Optional pro finish: cut the emblem in two felt colors, a base shape plus a smaller top shape.

Q: How do you make two capes look like a matching duo?
A: Same cape length, same emblem shape, inverted colors (your emblem is red-on-black, theirs is black-on-red). Matching shape plus inverted color reads as team instantly.

Q: Fabric glue or safety pins for the emblem?
A: Glue for the emblem (flat, permanent for the night), pins for anything you might reposition. Glue the emblem the night before so it cures.

### Cardboard Knight

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/cardboard-knight

Silver-painted cardboard armor and a pool-noodle sword.

Build time, effort: 60 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- Large cardboard boxes, 2 to 3 (make: collect spares)
- Silver acrylic paint, 1 bottle (buy: craft store, tempera paint works too)
- Foam brush or paintbrush, 1 wide (own, or buy: craft store)
- 1 pool noodle (buy: toy store or dollar store)
- Gray duct tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
- Black marker, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Safety: An adult should handle the heavy cutting. Cut generous eye holes in the helmet so vision stays clear.
2. Draw every piece on the cardboard before cutting: chest plate, back plate, shoulders, helmet.
3. Cut the helmet eye holes wide. Cardboard cannot be added back.
4. A knight who cannot see is a hazard.
5. Cut all the pieces.
6. Paint every armor piece silver.
7. Let the paint dry fully.
8. Add rivet dots and edge lines with the black marker.
9. Tape the plates together so they hinge at the shoulders.
10. Wrap the pool noodle in gray duct tape for the sword.
11. Put the armor on over dark clothes.
12. Carry the noodle sword.
13. Optional pro finish: tape a red crepe-paper plume to the helmet top.

Q: How do you keep cardboard armor from falling apart?
A: Gray duct tape hinges at the shoulders and sides, tape both sides of each joint. The tape is the armor's skeleton; the cardboard is just the skin.

Q: What is the safest sword option?
A: A pool noodle wrapped in gray duct tape. It looks metallic in photos and cannot hurt anyone. Never use wood or real metal, even blunted.

### Cat & Mouse

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/cat-mouse

Cat ears versus mouse ears. Spend the night chasing each other.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- 2 headbands (buy: dollar store)
- 1 sheet black craft felt, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, construction paper works too)
- 1 sheet gray craft felt, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, construction paper works too)
- Black eyeliner pencil or non-toxic face paint, 1 (buy: toy store)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Tape, 1 roll
- Pink felt, 1 small triangle (optional, for inner ears; buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Cut one paper ear first: triangles for the cat, rounds for the mouse.
2. Check both ears against the headbands.
3. Cut two triangle ears from the black felt.
4. Cut two round ears from the gray felt, about 3 inches across.
5. Safety: Keep the eyeliner clear of the eyes.
6. Put on the headbands.
7. Draw whiskers on both faces with the eyeliner pencil.
8. Optional pro finish: glue a pink felt triangle inside each ear.

Q: How do you tell the cat and mouse apart at a glance?
A: Cat gets triangle ears plus drawn whiskers; mouse gets round ears plus a pink nose dot. Different ear shape plus one face detail each, never rely on color alone.

Q: Eyeliner or face paint for whiskers?
A: Eyeliner pencil for teens and adults (precise), non-toxic face paint for kids (gentler). Either way keep it clear of the actual eyes.

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/cereal-crew

Solid-color clothes plus a cereal-box front you decorate.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

- Tape, 1 roll

Steps:
1. Each person invents a cereal name.
2. Open the box along the side seam.
3. Flatten it before cutting.
4. Cut the front panel off an empty cereal box.
5. Safety: Cut the box panel slowly. Keep fingers clear of the scissors.

### Cheerleader

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/cheerleader

Team colors and pom-poms made from cut plastic bags.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- Team-color t-shirt and skirt or shorts, 1 set (own)
- 4 to 6 white plastic grocery bags (make: save from home)
- Hair ribbon in a team color, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Rubber bands or tape, 1 pack (own)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Safety: Cut the bags up right away. Keep whole bags away from very small children.
2. Stack 2 to 3 white plastic grocery bags.
3. Cut them into long strips.
4. Stop 3 inches from one end.
5. Do NOT cut all the way through, or the pom-pom falls apart.
6. Roll the uncut end tightly.
7. Wrap it with a rubber band or tape.
8. Fluff the strips.
9. Make a second pom-pom the same way.
10. Pull on the team-color t-shirt and skirt or shorts.
11. Tie the hair ribbon in a bow.
12. Carry a pom-pom in each hand.
13. Optional pro finish: roll a sheet of paper into a cone megaphone and tape it.

Q: How fluffy should the pom-poms be?
A: Fluff each strip individually after rolling the handle, the fluffing is 80% of the look. Flat strips read as trash bag; fluffed strips read as pom-pom.

Q: Are plastic bag pom-poms safe for toddlers?
A: Cut the bags up right away and keep whole bags away from very small children. For under-3s, use tissue paper pom-poms instead.

### Chill Painter with Fro

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/chill-painter

A big brown afro wig, denim shirt, and a palette you painted yourself.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Big brown afro wig, 1 (buy: costume aisle or online)
- Denim shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Jeans, 1 (own)
- Cardboard for the palette, 1 sheet (make: from a shipping box)
- Acrylic paints in bright colors, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Toy paintbrush, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut a palette shape from the cardboard, with a thumb hole.
2. Dab the bright paints onto the palette.
3. Let it dry completely.
4. Wear the denim shirt and jeans with the afro wig.
5. Carry the palette and brush everywhere.
6. Narrate happy little details about the party.
7. Safety: Let the palette dry fully before the party so wet paint never touches clothes or furniture.
8. Optional pro finish: compliment one thing about every costume you see, in character.

Q: How do you keep the wig on all night?
A: Wear a wig cap underneath and pin the wig at four points. Afro wigs are top-heavy and slide without pins.

### Chipmunk Trio

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/chipmunk-trio

Letter sweaters, felt ears, and whiskers for a singing trio of chipmunks.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Red, blue, and green sweaters or sweatshirts, 1 each (buy: thrift store)
- Iron-on letters A, S, T, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Brown felt for ears, 3 pairs worth, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Headbands, 3 (buy: dollar store)
- Brown eyeliner for whiskers and a nose, 1 (buy: drugstore)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Lay the sweaters flat.
2. Position the letters on each chest.
3. Have each person confirm their letter before you heat the iron.
4. Iron-on letters cannot be moved once pressed.
5. Iron A onto the red sweater, S onto the blue, T onto the green.
6. Let them cool flat.
7. Cut round ears from the brown felt.
8. Glue one pair of ears to each headband.
9. Wear the letter sweaters with the ear headbands.
10. Draw three whisker dots and a nose on each cheek.
11. Safety: Let an adult use the iron. Keep the eyeliner clear of the eyes.
12. Line up tallest to shortest.
13. Sing one note together for the photo.
14. Optional pro finish: stuff each cheek with a cotton ball for the group photo.

Q: Which chipmunk is which?
A: Red + A is the leader, blue + S is the cool one, green + T is the chubby one. Line up tallest to shortest in that order and the reference lands.

Q: No iron, can I still do the letters?
A: Yes: cut the letters from felt and fabric-glue them on, or safety-pin paper letters. Iron-on is cleanest, but glued felt survives the night.

### Chips & Guac

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/chips-guac

Green guac tunic with red tomato dots for one, giant triangle chip hat for the other.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 20 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Green t-shirt or tunic, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Tan t-shirt or tunic, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Red craft felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Yellow craft felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Tan craft felt, 2 sheets 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store, or use your own)
- Fabric glue, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Buy the felt and glue.
2. Pull a green and a tan t-shirt from the closet.
3. Guac: cut small circles from the red and yellow felt, about quarter size.
4. Glue the dots across the front of the green t-shirt.
5. Let the glue dry flat for 20 minutes.
6. Chip: cut a triangle from the tan felt, about 2 feet tall.
7. Glue the base of the triangle to the headband.

### Classic Ghost

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/classic-ghost

A white sheet with cut-out eyes.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 white flat sheet: twin size for kids under 8, full size for tweens and adults (make: use an old sheet; buy: thrift store)
- Black marker, thick tip, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- 2 small squares of black tulle or sheer fabric, about 4 inches each (optional, for see-through eyes; buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Pick the sheet: twin for a small kid, full for a big kid or adult. Bigger than you need is fine. Smaller is not.
2. Drape the sheet over the wearer.
3. Have them stand still.
4. Mark both eye spots with the marker while the sheet is on.
5. Take the sheet off.
6. Cut the eye holes small first, about the size of a quarter. You can widen them. You cannot shrink them.
7. Hold the sheet up.
8. Check the wearer can see through both holes.
9. Widen a little at a time.
10. Optional pro finish: tape a square of black tulle behind each hole.
11. Safety: Trim the bottom so the hem clears the ground by several inches, a dragging hem is what trips a kid on a dark sidewalk. Keep nothing tight around the neck.
12. Draw a wavy or smiling mouth below the eyes.
13. Drape the sheet back on and go.

Q: How do I make eye holes safely?
A: Mark them while the sheet is on the wearer, cut small first, and widen until they see clearly. Back with black tulle so the eyes look dark but stay see-through.

Q: What size sheet for a toddler ghost?
A: A twin flat sheet, trimmed short. Cut it shorter than feels right, toddlers trip on hems adults would clear.

### Coffee Cup

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/coffee-cup

White trash bag over a cardboard tube, brown lid hat.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- White trash bag or white sheet, 1 large (make: from home)
- Cardboard tube or large cylinder, 1 (make: from home)
- Brown paper or felt for the lid, 1 sheet (buy: craft store)
- Brown marker, 1 thick (buy: dollar store)

Steps:
1. Cut the arm holes first.
2. Then cut the head hole small.
3. Stretch the bag over the head to test before cutting bigger.
4. Cut the holes in the white trash bag for head and arms.
5. Safety: Cut the head hole wide enough. The wearer must see and breathe with ease.
6. This is the cup.
7. A head hole cut too big slides off the shoulders.
8. Draw a coffee shop logo on the front with brown marker.
9. Make the lid: cut a brown paper circle bigger than your head, with a sip hole.
10. Wear the bag.
11. Put the lid hat on top.
12. Optional pro finish: cut a cardboard sleeve, write a coffee-shop pun on it, and tape it around the torso.

Q: How do you keep a trash-bag costume from looking like a trash bag?
A: The lid and the logo do all the work. A brown lid hat plus a big drawn logo reads as coffee cup; without them it reads as trash bag.

Q: Is a trash bag safe to wear?
A: Cut generous head and arm holes before putting it on, never pull it over the face, and keep it away from very small children. A white sheet is the safer alternative for toddlers.

### Crowd Camouflage

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/crowd-camouflage

Gray hoodie, dark pants, blank expression. Vanish into any crowd.

Build time, effort: 5 min / Easy

Materials:
- Gray hoodie, 1 (own)
- Dark pants, 1 pair (own)
- Gray beanie, 1 (own, or buy: dollar store)
- Blank adhesive name tag, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Pen, 1 (own)

Steps:
1. Pull on the gray hoodie, hood up, the dark pants, and the gray beanie.
2. Stick the blank name tag on the chest of the hoodie.
3. Write nothing on the tag. That is the joke.
4. Keep a blank face.
5. Blend into the back of every group photo.
6. Optional pro finish: stand in the back row of every group photo with a perfectly blank expression.

Q: What is the joke of this costume?
A: You are camouflaged as a random background person, the blank name tag, the gray hoodie, the neutral face. It is funniest in big group photos where nobody notices you until the second look.

Q: How do you make it read as a costume, not just gray clothes?
A: The blank name tag is the tell. Without it you are just underdressed; with it, people get the bit.

### Cupcake

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/cupcake

Brown tunic for the wrapper, white pillowcase for frosting, cherry on top.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Brown t-shirt or tunic for the wrapper, 1 (make: from closet)
- White pillowcase for the frosting, 1 (make: from home)
- Red pom-pom or ball for the cherry, 1 about 2 inches (buy: craft store)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Put on the brown shirt.
2. Drape the white pillowcase over your head and shoulders.
3. Mark where your eyes are while wearing it.
4. Take it off.
5. Cut the eye holes small first, then widen.
6. Safety: Cut the eye holes wide. Your child must see and breathe with ease.
7. Cut the bottom edge in waves.
8. Glue the red pom-pom on top as the cherry.
9. Fluff the pillowcase edges like frosting swirls.
10. Optional pro finish: dot the pillowcase with fabric markers for sprinkles.

Q: How do you keep the pillowcase frosting on your head?
A: It drapes, no attachment needed if the pillowcase is adult-size on a kid. For adults, pin it to a headband at the forehead so it does not slide.

Q: What is the wrapper part?
A: The brown shirt is the cupcake liner. Vertical marker stripes on the brown shirt sell the wrapper ridges.

### Daisy

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/daisy

A yellow petal headband and a green dress: a walking flower.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Yellow craft foam sheets, 2 (buy: craft store)
- Brown craft foam for the flower center, 1 sheet (buy: craft store)
- Green dress, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store, or use your own)
- Glue, 1 tube craft glue (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut 10 to 12 petal shapes from the yellow craft foam.
2. Arrange the petals around the headband dry before gluing.
3. Glue the petals in a ring, tips out.
4. Glue the brown foam circle in the center.
5. Safety: Let the glue dry fully before wearing.
6. Wear the flower headband with the green dress.
7. Optional pro finish: dot the brown center with yellow fabric paint dots.

Q: How many petals does a daisy need?
A: Ten to twelve. Fewer looks sparse, more looks like a sunflower. Overlap them slightly so no headband shows through.

Q: Foam or felt for the petals?
A: Craft foam holds its shape and springs back; felt flops by hour two. Foam looks twice as good.

### Deadpan Diva

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/deadpan-diva

Black dress, two braids, pale makeup, and a stare that ends conversations.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Black dress, 1 (own)
- Very pale foundation or white non-toxic face paint, 1 (buy: toy store)
- Dark eyeliner and lipstick, 1 set (own, or buy: dollar store)
- 2 hair ties (own)
- Thin black ribbon, 1 short length (optional, for the choker; buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Braid the hair into two tight braids.
2. Buy the white non-toxic face paint if needed.
3. Test the pale foundation on the jawline first.
4. Blend fully.
5. Put the pale foundation on evenly.
6. Blend into the neck.
7. Add the dark eyeliner and lipstick.
8. Put on the black dress.
9. Fold the arms.
10. Hold the stare.
11. Use skin-safe makeup.
12. Wash it all off before bed.
13. Optional pro finish: add a thin black ribbon choker.
14. Safety: Add reflective tape or a glow stick and carry a flashlight for visibility at night.

Q: How do you get the braids right?
A: Two tight braids, middle part, pulled flat against the head. Loose or messy braids break the severe look, tight is the whole point.

Q: How do you take off heavy pale makeup?
A: Wash with a gentle cleanser, not just water, stage-white needs soap. Moisturize after; pale foundation is drying. Never sleep in it.

### Decades Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/decades-crew

Each person picks a decade and dresses from their own closet.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Each person's own closet clothes (make: use what you own)
- 1 printed decade card per person, e.g. 70s, 80s, 90s, cardstock or paper (make: hand-letter on paper)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Tape, 1 roll or safety pins, 1 pack
- Hair gel or spray, 1 (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Everyone picks a different decade from their closet clothes.
2. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when trimming the decade cards.
3. Letter each decade card big, 4-inch letters at least.
4. Tape a decade card to each chest.
5. Build each look with closet props only.
6. Bell-bottoms and a headband for the 70s.
7. Neon and high socks for the 80s.
8. Flannel tied at the waist for the 90s.
9. Style hair with gel to match the decade.
10. Keep props light so the looks last all night.
11. Optional pro finish: give each decade one era prop, like a fake vinyl record for the 70s.

Q: How do you keep decades from looking random?
A: Assign decades first so no two people pick the same one, and give each person ONE signature item (neon for 80s, flannel for 90s). One signature item per decade beats five vague ones.

Q: What is the fastest 90s look?
A: Flannel tied around the waist over a plain tee, jeans, and a middle part. Three items, all from a closet, reads instantly.

### Demon Boy Band

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/demon-boy-band

Matching streetwear-idol outfits with glowing patterns for your whole boy band.

Build time, effort: 40 min + 2 hrs drying / Easy

Materials:
- Oversized black or white t-shirt per person, 1 each (make: from closet)
- Baggy pants per person, 1 pair each (make: from closet)
- Neon fabric paint, 1 small bottle each in 2 colors (buy: craft store)
- Temporary tattoos or 1 neon eyeliner pencil (buy: drugstore)
- Toy microphone per person, 1 each (buy: dollar store)
- Hair gel, 1 travel-size tube (make: from the bathroom)
- Sunglasses per person, 1 each, optional (make: from the drawer)

Steps:
1. Pick the pattern together.
2. Sketch it on paper first.
3. Test the neon paint on an inside seam first.
4. Paint matching patterns on everyone: lightning on sleeves, circles on chest.
5. Keep all paint on the clothes, off faces and away from eyes.
6. Let the paint dry flat for 2 hours.
7. Put neon eyeliner or tattoos on cheeks and hands.
8. Style hair up and forward with the gel.
9. Safety: Keep paint off faces and away from eyes.
10. Wear the matching streetwear.
11. Carry a toy microphone each.
12. Line up shoulder to shoulder for the album-cover pose.
13. Optional pro finish: give every member the same tattoo on the same cheek.
14. Safety: Add reflective tape or a glow stick and carry a flashlight for visibility at night.

Q: Will neon fabric paint glow without a black light?
A: No, it needs a black light to pop. Without one it still reads as bright neon color, so check what the venue has before you count on the glow.

Q: How do you keep the paint from cracking when they move?
A: Paint thin lines, not thick blobs, and let it dry the full 2 hours. Thick paint cracks the first time an arm bends.

### Deviled Egg

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/deviled-egg

White shirt with a felt yolk, devil horns, and a red tail. Half egg, half devil.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 white t-shirt (buy: craft store, or use one you own)
- 1 sheet yellow felt, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- 2 sheets red felt, 9x12 inches each (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- 1 red headband (buy: dollar store)
- 2 red pipe cleaners, 12 inches each (buy: craft store; twisted strips of red paper work too)
- Scissors, 1 pair; tape, 1 roll or glue, 1 bottle
- Red face paint or lipstick, 1 (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the felt.
2. Draw the yolk oval on paper first.
3. Hold it against the t-shirt to check the size.
4. Cut the oval from the yellow felt.
5. Cut it bigger, not smaller.
6. Tape or glue the yellow oval to the chest of the white t-shirt.
7. Twist the two red pipe cleaners into small horns.
8. Tape the horns to the red headband.
9. Cut a long pointed tail from the red felt, about 18 inches.
10. Tape the tail to the back of the t-shirt at two points.
11. Sit down once to make sure the tail clears the chair.
12. Optional pro finish: cut a jagged white felt ring around the yolk.

Q: How big should the yolk be?
A: Dinner-plate size, centered on the chest. Smaller than a dessert plate disappears across a room.

Q: How do you keep the tail from flopping?
A: Tape it at two points, shoulder blades and lower back. One tape point lets it swing; two keeps it standing.

---

### Dino Herd

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/dino-herd

Green ponchos with felt spikes and stuffed-sock tails.

Build time, effort: 30 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 green poncho or green bedsheet per person, about 50x60 inches (buy: craft store or online)
- 1 sheet green felt per person, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- 1 old sock per person, white or colored (make: use one you own)
- Scrap fabric or cotton balls for stuffing, about 1 cup per person (make: use what you own)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube, or 6 safety pins per person (buy: craft store or dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Buy one green poncho and one green felt sheet per person.
2. Raid the sock drawer for an old sock.
3. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the green felt.
4. Cut one paper triangle first.
5. Check the size on the poncho.
6. Cut 8 to 10 felt triangles per person, all from the paper template.
7. Pin the triangles in a row down the back of the poncho.
8. Stuff the old sock with scrap fabric.
9. Pin the sock to the back waistband of the poncho as the tail.
10. Wear the poncho over a t-shirt and jeans.
11. Pin the spikes and tail flat so they do not poke anyone.
12. Optional pro finish: pin a row of small felt spikes along the sock tail too.

Q: How do you keep the spikes upright in a crowd?
A: Pin each spike at two points, base and middle, flat against the poncho so they do not poke anyone. Flat-pinned spikes survive hugs.

Q: What size poncho for small kids?
A: Cut a twin bedsheet in half for kids under 8. A full poncho drags on small kids and trips them.

### Dino Rangers

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/dino-rangers

Khaki outfits for the grown-ups, dino hoods for the kids. Leash a toy raptor.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- Khaki shirt, 1, and khaki pants, 1 pair, per grown-up (make: use what you own)
- Green hoodie per child, 1 each (buy: thrift store, or use one you own)
- White paper or card, 2 sheets (make: use what you own)
- 1 toy dinosaur or plush per kid (buy: toy store)
- Ribbon or string, 18 inches per kid (make: use what you own)
- Tape, 1 roll and scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Dress the grown-ups in the khaki shirt and pants.
2. Roll the sleeves.
3. Buy or dig out a green hoodie for each kid, the toy dinosaur, and the ribbon.
4. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the white paper.
5. Draw the eye spots on paper first.
6. Hold them against the hood to check.
7. Cut two oval eye spots from the white paper, about 3 inches tall.
8. Cut them smaller than you think, or they slide off the hood.
9. Safety: Skip small plastic dinosaur toys for kids under three, since they are a choking hazard.
10. Loop the ribbon around the toy dinosaur like a leash.
11. Tie the other end to the kid's wrist.
12. Keep the leash short.
13. Optional pro finish: write each kid's dinosaur name on tape and stick it on the khaki shirt.

Q: Is the wrist leash safe for a kid?
A: Yes if you use a loose loop tied over the jacket sleeve, never tight on bare skin, and keep it short so it cannot catch on playground equipment.

Q: What if we have no khaki clothes?
A: Any neutral shirt and pants work: tan, olive, or beige. Roll the sleeves twice and the field-guide look comes through.

### Dino Tourist

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/dino-tourist

Hawaiian shirt, dino tail, camera around your neck, and a fanny pack. The meteor missed this one.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 Hawaiian shirt (buy: thrift store, or use your own)
- 1 fanny pack (own, or buy: thrift store)
- 1 plush dinosaur tail (buy: toy store or online)
- 1 toy camera, optional (own)
- 1 pair sunglasses, optional (own)

Steps:
1. Pull the Hawaiian shirt and fanny pack from the closet.
2. Clip or pin the plush tail to your waistband at the back.
3. Safety: Use the clip if you can. Pin backs must face cloth, not skin.
4. Hang the toy camera around your neck.
5. Put on the sunglasses.
6. Ask strangers to take your picture.
7. Complain about the meteor.
8. Optional pro finish: tuck a folded paper map into the fanny pack and let it stick out.

Q: How do you attach the tail so it stays on?
A: Clip or pin it to the waistband at the back center with two safety pins through the tail's seam. One pin spins; two pins hold.

Q: How do you make it read as dinosaur, not just tourist?
A: The tail does all the work. Without it you are just a tourist: wear it high on the waistband where people see it from the side.

### Dinosaur Family

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/dinosaur-family

Matching dino-hoodie sweatsuits for the whole crew, spikes down every back.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 green sweatsuit per person (buy: discount store, or use one you own)
- 1 sheet green felt per person, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Fabric glue, 1 tube, or 6 safety pins per person (buy: craft store or dollar store)
- Green face paint, non-toxic, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Buy one green sweatsuit and one sheet of green felt per person.
2. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the green felt.
3. Trace your palm on paper.
4. Use it as the triangle template.
5. Cut 8 to 10 triangles from the green felt per person.
6. Glue or pin the triangles in a row down the back of the sweatsuit.
7. Paint green spots on each cheek.
8. Keep the paint clear of the eyes.
9. Put the sweatsuit on over regular clothes.
10. Pin the spikes flat to the hood so they stay put.
11. Optional pro finish: glue two small white felt triangles to the hood cuffs as claws.

Q: How do you keep the spikes from flopping?
A: Pin them flat against the hood so they point back, not up. Spikes pinned upward on soft fleece flop by the second photo.

Q: Will the face paint stain?

### The Doctor & the Bride

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/doctor-bride

Green face paint and neck bolts for one; tall streaked wig and torn gown for the other.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 old dark suit or jacket (make: use what you own)
- Green face paint, non-toxic, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)
- 2 plastic neck bolts, costume style (buy: craft store; foil-covered cardboard tubes work too)
- 1 white dress or old white sheet (make: use what you own)
- White hair spray, 1 can (buy: drugstore)
- Tape, 1 roll or glue, 1 bottle
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Dark eye shadow, 1 (make: use what you own)

Steps:
1. Safety: Keep face paint away from the eyes, and patch-test it first on sensitive skin. Wash it off the same night.
2. The Doctor: paint the face and neck green.
3. Tape the two plastic bolts to the sides of the neck.
4. Wear the dark suit with the collar up.
5. Put the white dress on.
6. Mark the tear line with tape.
7. Knee length for walking, longer for photos.
8. Tear the bottom hem into strips by hand.
9. Start with small tears.
10. Smudge dark eye shadow under the eyes.
11. Optional pro finish: smudge a little green face paint onto the bride's neck and hands too.

Q: How do you keep the neck bolts on?
A: Tape each bolt to the collar, not the skin, with two strips of fashion tape or bandage tape. Skin-safe tape only: never superglue.

Q: Will white hair spray wash out?
A: Yes with one shampoo. Spray it outside, keep it off clothes, and test a strand first on very dark hair since it can tint temporarily.

### Donut

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/donut

Pink cardboard ring with sprinkles, worn like a sandwich board.

Build time, effort: 35 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 large cardboard box, about 24x24 inches flat (make: from home)
- Pink paint, 1 small bottle (buy: craft store)
- Felt sprinkles, 12 to 15 small pieces, or sticker sprinkles (buy: craft store)
- Ribbon or string, 4 feet (make: from home)
- Scissors, 1 pair and glue, 1 bottle

Steps:
1. Draw the donut circle on the cardboard first.
2. Check it fits over the head: about 30 inches across, hole about 12 inches.
3. Cut the center hole smaller than the head first, then widen.
4. Safety: Cut the cardboard slowly. Keep fingers clear of the scissors.
5. A too-big hole slides off the shoulders.
6. Paint it pink.
7. Let it dry.
8. Glue on felt sprinkles or stickers in bright colors.
9. Attach ribbon to the top.
10. Wear it like a sandwich board.
11. Optional pro finish: paint a thin brown ring around the center hole.

Q: How do you wear a big cardboard donut comfortably?
A: Hang it from two ribbon straps like a sandwich board at waist height, not neck height. Waist height clears doorways and lets the arms move.

Q: How long does the pink paint take to dry?
A: About 1 hour for acrylic on cardboard. Paint the night before: wearing it damp smears pink onto every hug.

### Donut & Coffee

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/donut-coffee

Pink frosted ring tunic for one, takeout coffee cup for the other.

Build time, effort: 35 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- White t-shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Brown t-shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Pink craft felt, 2 sheets 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Cardboard ring for the donut, 1 large (make: from a shipping box)
- Tan fabric or paper to cover the ring (own, or buy: craft store)
- Cardboard for the coffee cup, 1 sheet (make: from a shipping box)
- Brown acrylic paint, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- White paper for the cup lid, 1 sheet (buy: dollar store)
- Tape, 1 roll
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Ribbon for straps, about 2 yards (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Buy the felt and paint.
2. Pull a white and a brown t-shirt from the closet.
3. Donut: cut a large ring from the cardboard, about 2 feet across.
4. Cut a 10-inch hole in the middle.
5. Cover the ring with tan fabric or paper.
6. Glue a pink felt ring on top for the frosting.
7. Dot it with small felt sprinkles.
8. Tape ribbon loops to the ring.
9. Wear it over the white t-shirt.
10. Coffee: roll cardboard into a tall cup.
11. Tape the seam.
12. Paint the cup brown.
13. Let it dry.
14. Fold the white paper into a lid.
15. Tape it to the top of the cup.
16. Wear the cup like a sandwich board over the brown t-shirt.
17. Safety: Round all cardboard edges, and keep the donut hole big enough that arms move freely.
18. Optional pro finish: the coffee person links arms with the donut person.

Q: How do you cut a clean donut ring?
A: Trace a large mixing bowl for the outside and a salad plate for the hole. Cut the hole first while the cardboard is whole, then the outside.

Q: How do you keep the frosting ring from peeling?
A: Glue the pink felt in sections and press each for 30 seconds. Felt glued all at once bubbles and lifts.

### Dragon Rider Duo

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/dragon-rider-duo

A viking rider and a cardboard dragon, ready to fly over the neighborhood.

Build time, effort: 60 min + 30 min drying / Medium

Materials:
- 1 brown t-shirt and 1 pair dark pants for the rider (make: from closet)
- Gray felt, 2 yards, or 1 old gray blanket for the dragon tunic (buy: craft store or thrift store)
- 1 large cardboard box for wings and tail (make: collect spares)
- Black and yellow craft foam, 1 sheet each for the dragon eyes (buy: craft store)
- 1 faux-fur vest or brown scarf for the rider (make: from closet)
- 1 headband for the dragon eyes
- Scissors, tape, and string, 6 feet (make: household tools)

Steps:
1. Draw the wing shape on paper first.
2. Hold it against the dragon person's back: shoulder to hip.
3. Cut two wing shapes and a long tail from the cardboard box.
4. Cut the wings smaller than the paper test, not bigger.
5. Big wings hit every doorway.
6. Tape all cut edges smooth before wearing.
7. Glue the black and yellow foam eyes to a headband.
8. The rider wears the faux-fur vest over the brown t-shirt.
9. Safety: Keep wing tips above waist height and tape all cardboard edges smooth so nobody gets scratched.
10. Rider stands in front, arms out like steering.
11. Dragon crouches behind with wings spread.
12. Take the flying photo.
13. Optional pro finish: tape a row of small cardboard triangles along the dragon's shoulders.

Q: How do you keep cardboard wings up?
A: Tape them to the gray felt tunic, not the person, with wide packing-tape tabs on both sides. Taped wings stay up for hours; glued wings peel.

Q: What is the best pose for the photo?
A: Rider stands in front with arms out like steering, dragon crouches behind with wings spread. The crouch sells the size difference.

### Emerald Witch

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/emerald-witch

An all-green-everything gown, dramatic makeup, and a pointy hat gone couture.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- 1 long green dress, or green fabric, 3 yards (buy: fabric store)
- 1 sheet black cardboard, 22x28 inches, for the hat (buy: craft store; a box painted black works too)
- Green face paint, non-toxic, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)
- Black eyeliner, 1, and dark green eye shadow, 1 (buy: drugstore)
- Hot glue gun with glue sticks, 1 set and scissors, 1 pair
- 1 broom from home for a prop (make: use what you own)

Steps:
1. Safety: Let an adult handle the hot glue, since the nozzle and glue get very hot.
2. Sew or hot glue the green fabric into a long gown.
3. Leave the hem ragged.
4. Measure the head first.
5. Roll the black cardboard into a tall cone.
6. Tape it loosely to check the fit.
7. Glue a wide cardboard brim to the base.
8. Test the cone shape dry first.
9. Hot glue sets fast and cannot be moved.
10. Paint the face green.
11. Draw on the black eyeliner and the dark green eye shadow.
12. Carry the broom bristle-up so it does not trip anyone.
13. Optional pro finish: fray the gown hem with 2-inch slits every few inches.

Q: How do you get green face paint off?
A: Wash with a gentle cleanser and soap, not just water: green needs soap. Moisturize after, and patch-test on the jawline first if skin is sensitive.

Q: What if I cannot sew the gown?
A: Hot glue works: fold the fabric around the body and glue the seam. It holds for one night and nobody sees the seam from the front.

### Emoji Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/emoji-crew

Everyone picks an emoji: a yellow tee plus a big printed face.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 yellow t-shirt per person (buy: craft store, or use one you own)
- 1 large white paper plate, 10-inch, or cardboard circle per person (make: use what you own)
- Markers in black, red, and blue, 1 set (make: use what you own)
- Scissors, 1 pair and tape, 1 roll

Steps:
1. Buy yellow t-shirts if the crew does not own them.
2. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the paper plates or cardboard circles.
3. Draw the emoji on the paper plate in pencil first.
4. Go over it with the markers.
5. Trim the plate only where it hangs past the design.
6. Cut small.
7. Tape the paper plate to the chest of the yellow t-shirt.
8. Gather the crew in a row for photos.
9. Keep the plates taped flat.
10. Optional pro finish: outline the whole plate edge in black marker.

Q: How do you pick emojis for the crew?
A: Assign them first so nobody duplicates. Crowd-pleasers: heart-eyes, laughing-crying, and the sunglasses face. Let the shyest person take the poop emoji: it gets the biggest laugh.

Q: How do you keep the plate from swinging?
A: Tape it at four points, top, bottom, and both sides, so it sits flat on the chest. Two tape points lets it flap all night.

### Emotion Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/emotion-crew

One loud color per person: each of you is a different emotion.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 solid bright color outfit per person: yellow, blue, red, green, purple, or orange (buy: a set at a thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Face paint matching each outfit color, 1 per person (buy: drugstore)
- 1 white poster board per person (buy: dollar store)
- Markers, 1 set (make: from the house)
- Colored hair spray matching each outfit, 1 can per person, optional (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Pull one loud solid-color outfit per person from the closet.
2. Buy the face paint, poster board, and markers.
3. Each person picks an emotion.
4. Write it big on poster board.
5. Paint a simple face design in the matching color.
6. Mist hair with the matching color spray if you like.
7. Safety: Use the spray outside or near fresh air. Keep paint clear of the eyes.
8. Wear the full one-color outfit with the emotion sign.
9. Group up in a row like the control panel.
10. Optional pro finish: paint each face design in the matching outfit color only.

Q: How do you stop two people picking the same emotion?
A: Assign emotions before anyone shops: Joy, Sadness, Anger, Fear, Disgust, Anxiety, Envy, Embarrassment, Ennui. First come first served, written on a list.

Q: How big should the emotion sign be?
A: Letter it 4 inches tall minimum on the poster board. The sign is the costume's label: if nobody can read it across the room, it is decoration.
